column1: # Start permissive; promote a rule to FAIL once the app is clean for it. Every
# IGNORE must carry a reason — an unexplained IGNORE is how a real finding hides.
# Triaged 2026-08-24 against a PRODUCTION build (npm run build && npm start).
# Do not triage against `npm run dev`: dev adds 'unsafe-eval' to script-src and
# serves react-refresh.js, so a dev scan invents findings prod does not have.

column3: Incident/cache headers on dynamic routes — review, don't block
Cross-domain JS: checkout.razorpay.com + clerk-js, by design. The CSP host allowlist is the control, not SRI. Re-check if a NEW origin appears here.
Anti-clickjacking — CSP frame-ancestors 'none' is set; verify on all routes
X-Content-Type-Options — already set in next.config.mjs; verify coverage
X-Powered-By fixed via poweredByHeader:false. Promoted to FAIL so it cannot regress silently.
Non-storable content is DELIBERATE: Cache-Control no-store on authenticated and payment pages. A cacheable order page is the actual bug.
style-src 'unsafe-inline' is accepted (no Tailwind, inline styles are the design system). NEVER ignore this rule — it also fires on script-src unsafe-eval, which must never appear in prod.
Permissions-Policy set in next.config.mjs. Coverage verified on HTML, _next static assets AND 404 responses, so FAIL is safe and stops a regression.
Base64 disclosure — matches inside minified Next chunks (asset hashes, inlined data URIs), not secrets. Re-check if it ever fires on an HTML response carrying user data.
Timestamp disclosure — Next asset hashes, not sensitive
Modern web message manifest — not applicable
SRI missing on checkout.razorpay.com — DO NOT "fix". Razorpay ships new checkout.js without notice; a pinned hash would break every payment on their next deploy.
COEP/CORP not set. require-corp would break the cross-origin Razorpay Checkout iframe. Revisit only with a live test on every rail.
Sec-Fetch-Dest missing — ZAP is reporting that ITS OWN requests lack the header. Not an app defect; browsers always send it.
